text:
support-ops: FYI customer escalation hitting hosted inference — multiple tenants reporting 5xx and timeouts since ~12:02 UTC. High volume of gateway 504s and connection timeouts. Seen in SLO alerts + a direct report from AcmeCorp support ticket. Repro snippets below. Investigating autoscaling issues (suspect HPA/KEDA not ramping fast enough, pod warmups slow).

andre: can you paste the gateway error patterns? stack traces or kube events? also which model(s) affected? @eng-oncall please ping if you're on call. :warning:

support-ops: logs from gateway (scrubbed):
```
2026-03-15T12:03:11Z gateway ERROR request_id=xyz123 upstream_error="dial tcp 10.42.5.21:8080: connect: connection refused" path=/v1/generate status=504 latency=12.34s
2026-03-15T12:03:12Z gateway ERROR request_id=xyz124 upstream_error="rpc error: code = Unknown desc = model load timeout" path=/v1/chat status=500 latency=30.01s
2026-03-15T12:04:05Z gateway WARN token=acct-abc auth=401 retry=3
```

support-ops: quick curl we ran to replicate (timed out):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"ggml-large","prompt":"hello","max_tokens":256}' --max-time 10 -v
```

mia: I'm seeing KEDA ScaledObject activity but pods not becoming Ready. KEDA scaled up from 3->12 around 12:04, HPA shows target CPU exceeded but new pods stuck in ContainerCreating/Init. kube events show mounts failing intermittently.

sre-bot: Event: Pod/model-server-87cfd Pending -> Warning FailedMount: MountVolume.MountDevice failed for volume "models-pvc" : rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded.

jordan: looks like model volume (NFS) warmup time is the bottleneck — model load takes 25-40s before server responds. With default request timeout 15s clients see 504s. For small models we usually hit 3-5s but these bigger ones need prefetch.

andre: can someone run these commands and attach outputs?
```
kubectl -n inference get hpa,deploy,po -l app=model-server -o wide
kubectl -n inference describe scaledobject <scaledobject-name>
kubectl -n inference get events --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 200
```

eng-oncall: running quick checks. KEDA scaled OK but node autoscaler only added nodes after ~45s. New pods scheduled but PVC attach to NFS timed out (we're hitting mount timeout of 30s). Also saw ImagePullBackOff on one instance due to transient registry throttling. I'm going to bump HPA.minReplicas and pin a fallback routing rule to the smaller model.

billing: note — some customers saw intermittent 401s around 12:03 caused by token rotation job overlapping with high traffic. Those 401s triggered client retries which amplified load. We're validating token rollout windows.

qa: can reproduce locally with a scripted load targeting model endpoints with cold server pool: steps:
1) start a pool of 2 replicas
2) run vegeta: `echo "POST /v1/generate" | vegeta attack -duration=30s -rate=50 -header "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -body request.json`
3) observe initial 5xx/504s until pods become Ready

support-ops: temporary mitigations applied at 12:10 UTC:
- increased HPA.minReplicas from 2 -> 8 for affected deployment (patched and applied)
- patched routing to favor smaller model variant for eligible customers
- opened a short-term circuit at gateway to return 429 earlier to reduce thundering herd
- engaged infra to check NFS mount/registry throughput

andre: thanks. Jordan — can you propose a persistent fix? Options: pre-warm model cache during scale events, reduce model load time with quantized artifacts, or adjust KEDA scaler thresholds to trigger earlier. Also consider lowering client timeout or increasing gateway upstream timeout to 60s for heavy models.

jordan: Proposed long-term plan (draft):
- implement async prefetch/shard preloader on new node onboarding (pre-warm model weights)
- add an explicit coldstart lifecycle probe: return 202 until model is fully ready so gateway can retry to other replicas instead of blocking clients
- adjust scaler to use queueLength external metric and lower activationThreshold by 30% during peak windows
- coordinate with infra to migrate model storage to faster block-backed storage for hot models
I'll draft PRs for runtime changes this afternoon.

mia: immediate follow-ups for SRE/infra:
- investigate NFS mount timeouts and increase mount timeout or migrate hot mounts (assigned infra: @sarah)
- check node pool scaling latency and reduce node provision min CPU/cloud-provider settings
- ensure image registry rate limits are within contract or add a mirror in region

billing: follow-up: we'll push token rotation schedule to low-traffic window and add a gradual rollout to avoid mass 401s causing retries.

eng-oncall: quick rollback plan if 5xx continues: route traffic to Dedicated nodes for affected customers, or enable read-only / degraded mode for non-critical endpoints. We can also temporarily reduce model sizes on hosted tier.

support-ops: customer update posted to ticket at 12:18: "We're aware of an incident causing increased timeouts for model inference. Our engineering team is actively mitigating by scaling pools and routing customers to smaller model variants. We'll follow up with postmortem." :thumbsup:

qa: creating a reproducible test in the eval harness and adding it to regression suite to avoid reintroducing slow scale-ups.

sarah: infra discovered NFS leader node experiencing IO saturation; moving hot PVCs to a faster disk now. ETA 30-45m.

andre: good. Please collect:
- kubectl outputs requested above
- KEDA ScaledObject YAML & metrics server outputs
- gateway trace for a failed request id (we have xyz123/xyz124)
- service latency histogram from 11:50-12:30 UTC
Attach them in this thread and in the incident tracker.

support-ops: next steps assigned: @jordan runtime (PRs for prewarm & lifecycle probe), @mia infra (mounts/node sizing), @billing adjust token rotation, @qa add regression, @support-ops continue customer comms. We'll reconvene in 30m unless critical regression.

sre-bot: Incident updated: severity=high -> mitigation_in_progress at 2026-03-15T12:11:00Z

support-ops: thanks everyone. capturing notes for postmortem and will label with root causes: (1) slow model warmup + NFS IO saturation; (2) autoscaler/node provisioning latency; (3) concurrent token rotation causing amplified retries.

andre: add follow-up action to add a canary pre-warm policy for top-10 heavy models and a dashboard showing pod Ready vs request arrival time.

support-ops: noted. logging final state at 12:30 UTC: errors reduced after mounting fix and bumping minReplicas; customer impact reduced but still monitoring. Will file postmortem template once incident closed.
